what: The command library reports an unknown option or unknown command by writing the process exit code itself and returning nothing, so a callable entry point cannot carry that outcome in its return value. Every caller must therefore apply a returned code only when it is non-zero, which is a rule each caller has to know and none can discover. The library is maintained by the same owner, so the fix belongs upstream: have its parse return the code it recorded.
evidence: confirmed by running the library directly — an unknown option leaves the return undefined and the process exit code at the usage value
